Hi Anna — thanks for the clear list. Long story short: yes, we can provide what you need and we can move fast to meet your 11/05 deadline. Below are the specifics and next steps.

1) SOC 2 Type II report: we have a 2025–2026 SOC 2 Type II report covering the control period 2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30. I'm attaching a redacted stub now; the full report is available under NDA.

2) Hosting & cross-border: we run three deployment modalities: Hosted (our public API), Dedicated (customer-reserved pools), and Private (VPC/on-prem). For EU data residency: Dedicated and Private can be deployed in EU regions (we commonly use eu-west-1 and eu-central-1). When configured for EU hosting, customer inference input, model content, and model KV caches remain in-region.

Notes about control plane: our default hosted control plane (auth, billing metadata) is in the US. For Dedicated/Private customers we provide an EU control-plane option or a private control plane so billing metadata and telemetry do not transit the US. If you need, we can provide specific wording about metadata flows for your DPA.

3) Bridge letter: we issue bridge letters when audit periods don't align. We can provide a signed letter attesting to continuity of key controls and whether any material changes occurred outside the audited period.

4) SIG / CAIQ: we have a completed CAIQ and an in-progress SIG pack; I'll include a completed SIG export for your procurement tooling.

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025-10-2026-09_stub.pdf (attached), eu-hosting-architecture-diagram.png (attached)

Kimberly (cc) is on security and can confirm encryption and KMS options. If you can send back the procurement SIG file and any specific sections of the DPA/legal language you care most about (e.g., SCCs, KMS residency), we'll prioritize those.

Best,
Jordan Blake

Anna — quick technical confirmation from Security.

- EU-hosted inference: available for Dedicated and Private customers. We run compute and persistent storage in the customer-chosen EU region. Live request/response traffic and KV caches remain in-region.
- Customer-managed keys (CMKs): supported for Dedicated and Private. Keys can be provisioned in an EU KMS (AWS KMS in eu-west-1 / eu-central-1).
- Hosted (public API): default deployment keeps inference data in the region you target, but the control plane (billing/usage aggregation) is served from our central control plane in the US. We can set up an EU control plane for enterprise customers under contract.
- Data exports / backups: by default backups are kept in-region for Dedicated/Private. Cross-region replication only occurs with explicit customer opt-in.

On bridge letters: we provide a templated letter that references the audited control set and the audit period, confirms no material control changes since the audit period end, and lists controls that operationally cover hosting/region choices. We can tailor wording to satisfy your risk team if you share the exact phrasing they require.

If you need a signed letter faster than the NDA/attestation cadence, we can generate a provisional bridge letter and follow up with the signed original after legal review.

-Kimberly
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Hi Anna — following up with the final artifacts and concrete answers so your team can close procurement. Attaching the items below and summarizing the answers to your follow-ups.

- Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025-10-2026-09_stub.pdf (redacted copy for procurement)

Summary answers: 
- Bridge letter: we will issue a bridge letter that references the SOC 2 Type II control set and the audit period (2025-10-01 through 2026-09-30). The letter will explicitly call out EU-hosted Dedicated/Private deployments (eu-west-1 and eu-central-1) as covered by the controls and will state that there were no material control changes affecting those controls since 2026-09-30. We can deliver a provisional PDF within 2 business days and a signed letter after legal review.
- KMS & scope: The SOC 2 report covers our cryptographic key management controls as operated by Redwood for standard hosted and Dedicated offerings. For customer-managed keys (CMKs) in Dedicated/Private deployments, the SOC 2 report documents the processes we use to support CMKs but a customer's own KMS tenancy is out of scope for our auditor. The SIG export indicates where we have compensating controls and where customer-side controls are expected.
- Metadata/control-plane flows: For Dedicated/Private configured with an EU control plane, billing metadata and telemetry remain in-region. For public hosted customers, billing aggregation and certain operational telemetry are processed in our US control plane; we can minimize PII sent for compliance purposes.

Next steps we suggest:
1) Review the attached SIG and DPA; if you want language edits in the bridge letter, send a redline and we'll incorporate.
2) If NDA required for the full SOC 2, let us know and we can route the full report via secure share within 24 hours of NDA.
3) We'll issue the provisional bridge letter by 2026-11-04 to meet your 11/05 COB deadline.

If you need a short joint call to finalize the bridge wording, I'm available tomorrow morning EU time.
